_comment: Known plug-and-play violations, recorded 2026-07-25 when check-integration-conformance
landed. This is the FIX BACKLOG, not a mute list: every entry is printed on every build,
and an entry that no longer reproduces fails the build so the list can only shrink.
Do NOT add entries to silence a new violation — fix the declaration or the runtime path.
2026-07-25: the five steer:* entries were removed when the model-locked routing clauses
were deleted from the email and calendar tool descriptions. test/tool-description-portability.test.ts
is now the runtime mirror of that check.
2026-07-25: authtype:google removed — google was narrowed to the endpoints an api_key can
actually satisfy, so the finding no longer reproduces. The hardcoded YouTube probe that was
the tell is gone too, replaced by declaration-driven probe headers.

known.note: HALF FIXED by C7a. email now declares transport 'smtp_imap' and getAgentContext() renders it as its email_* tools instead of an empty 'Base URL:' line, so the agent-prompt half of this finding no longer reproduces. What remains is the route half: /api/integrations/test still joins the smtp/imap pseudo-paths onto an empty baseUrl to build a nonsense probe URL. Fix (C7b): make the test route transport-aware. NOTE: this checker does not yet know the 'transport' field exists — its message still describes the agent-prompt half it no longer causes.

STALE — held only because the CHECKER is out of date, not because the defect reproduces. Its message asserts 'the install path persists only the primary', which stopped being true at C5: the route persists every declared credential, and C7a made email declare all nine (IMAP_* optional per E14). So IMAP_PASS IS now storable through the install path. The script even prints all nine while claiming only the primary is stored. Fix (C7b/C9): teach the checker that the install path persists the full declared list, then retire this entry.
